subject: SavePath renewal — request for one-time concessions and SLA add-on

Subject: Renewal proposal and urgent pricing/SLA ask

Hannah,

Thanks for the renewal package you sent Friday — Marco and I reviewed the numbers and the new usage forecast. We like the platform and want to continue, but there are two blockers for our CFO and procurement:

- A pricing gap vs. our internal budget (we need an additional ~20% in annual savings to hit our Q4 commit).
- We need a documented 99.95% SLA for inference latency (p50/p95 targets) and a credit mechanism for missed SLOs.

Procurement asked for a one-time concession to bridge the budget delta (term reset + a one-time credit would work). If we can agree to a 12-month term at the proposed volumes with a $60k one-time credit and a formal SLA addendum, they will sign by the end of next week.

I've attached our consolidated forecast and the internal approval notes. Can Redwood scope a formal SLA addendum and confirm whether a one-time credit is possible? We understand this is non-standard.

Appreciate a quick confirmation — savepath is a strategic account for us and we prefer to avoid a competitive procurement.

—Erin
Erin Cole
Head of AI Products | SavePath

Subject: RE: Fwd: Renewal proposal and urgent pricing/SLA ask — concession options

Hannah / team,

Quick take after a first-pass with finance:

- One-time credit: authorized up to $50k at manager level. Anything above requires VP executive sign-off.
- Term reset: we can offer a 12-month firm term but will require committing to their forecasted minimums; we should put a 10% underage fee to protect unit economics if they miss commit.
- SLA: legal is comfortable with a lightweight SLA addendum that documents p50/p95 latency objectives and a credit formula capped at a single monthly invoice credit (no recurring credits). We should avoid indemnity or uptime definitions that hit infra SLAs — keep it narrowly scoped to inference latency on Redwood-hosted endpoints.

If we request exec approval, recommendation: approve a one-time $60k concession but with the following guardrails:
- Deal-level cap: 1x month invoice credit and no future precedence (language included).
- Term: 12 months; commit floors as above.
- Finance to amortize credit across the first two invoices for revenue recognition.

I will draft the concession language and a short executive rationale. Priyom — please include net margin impact and a payback timeline.

—Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Sales Operations | Redwood Inference
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Oct 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: RE: concession options — P&L impact (summary)

Hannah / Vivek / Laura,

Attached a quick P&L and sensitivity table. Highlights:

- If we approve $60k one-time credit and the customer meets the forecasted commit, net margin decline in year 1 is ~7.8% versus baseline.
- If commit floors are enforced and they only hit 80% of forecast, effective margin drop increases to ~11.3%.
- Amortizing the credit across first two invoices reduces immediate revenue recognition pressure but does not materially change cash impact.

Recommendation: Approve $60k only if we get:
  * a signed 12-month term with commit floors (min monthly usage), and
  * an SLA addendum with a single credit cap and a 60-day cure period for any infra investigation.

I'll attach the spreadsheet (single-sheet) to the one-pager.

—Priyom
Priyom Das
Director, Finance — Revenue Operations | Redwood Inference

Subject: Executive approval request — SavePath renewal concession (one-time credit + SLA addendum)

Hi Exec team —

As discussed with sales ops and finance, SavePath (SavePath / DEAL-87421) is asking for a non-standard concession to execute a renewal this quarter. We are requesting your approval to proceed with the following limited exceptions:

Proposal (requested customer concession):
- One-time credit: $60,000 applied to first invoice (recommend amortize across first two invoices for accounting).
- Term: 12-month firm term; customer signs a commit with minimum monthly usage (10% underage fee if below commit).
- SLA addendum: 99.95% p95 inference latency target with single monthly invoice credit for missed SLOs (capped at one monthly invoice; 60-day investigation/cure period).

Rationale:
- SavePath is a strategic referenceable customer in embedded analytics; they have a validated expansion pipeline (see attached forecast).
- Competitive risk is high — procurement is evaluating a lower-cost incumbent and will escalate if we can't bridge budget delta quickly.
- Finance modeled a manageable margin impact (Priyom attached sensitivity).

Requested approvals / decisions:
1) Approve one-time credit of $60k (requires exec sign-off).
2) Approve SLA addendum scope as drafted and delegate to legal (Laura) to finalize language with the guardrails above.
3) If approved, delegate to Hannah to finalize commercial terms and execute by 2026-10-27 to meet procurement timeline.

Supporting materials attached: Redwood-SavePath-proposal-v3.pdf; SLA-addendum-draft.docx; SavePath_PnL_sensitivity.xlsx.

Thanks for a quick review — happy to join a 15-minute sync if helpful.

—Hannah
